what_happened: The job "Classify PR commits by content in athena land, not by trailers" (20261024-140624-ewbs) failed in the producer stage. The producer reached its fixed 1800-second deadline without finishing. The event lists no unmet acceptance criteria, no blocker or major findings and no failed checks. The job's record shows no partial result, so nothing was delivered. The job appears to belong to the landing and history-check work that earlier jobs on this branch also touched.
cause: The producer stage has a single fixed wall-clock limit and no way to see progress or stop early. When it hits the limit, everything it did is thrown away and the failure gives no hint of where the time went. Nothing before dispatch estimates whether the work fits in one run. A change to how landing classifies commits touches several places: the classifier, its callers, the history check and tests against realistic branch history. The critic does not hold the plan to a size bound, so a job that is too big for one run is accepted as is. The event holds no producer log, so the exact cause of the stall (an oversized scope, a test loop or a slow check) cannot be told. That gap is itself a cause: a timeout is recorded as a bare failure with no last activity.
prevention: Make the producer's deadline recoverable. (1) The producer commits checkpoints to the job branch and writes a short progress note as it goes. (2) On deadline, Athena keeps the partial work and the last note, marks the job "timed out with partial result" rather than a plain failure, and offers a continue run that starts from the checkpoint with a fresh deadline. (3) The planning critic checks each plan against a size bound (files touched, criteria count) and requires a split when it is exceeded. A split job and a continued job then fit within one run, and a timeout no longer loses all the work.
proposed_request: Make a producer deadline recoverable. When the producer stage reaches its time limit, keep the work done so far: commit the producer's working changes to the job branch, save the producer's last progress note and the tail of its log in the job record, and mark the job "timed out, partial result" instead of a plain failure. Add a way to continue such a job from that checkpoint with a fresh deadline, using the existing retry path. Show the progress note when the job is listed. Acceptance: a test with a fake producer that runs past the deadline shows the partial commit kept, the status distinct from a normal failure, and a continue run that starts from the checkpoint. Then retry the job "Classify PR commits by content in athena land, not by trailers" (20261024-140624-ewbs) from its checkpoint, or, if no checkpoint exists, as a new job. Keep the scope to the classifier. The test must use realistic branch history: records-only commits, owner-path commits and intervention commits.
